title: Fairway: A Way to Build Fair ML Software

edges.target: Optimized Preprocessing (Calmon et al.)
edges.ref: [33] F. Calmon, D. Wei, B. Vinzamuri, K. Natesan Ramamurthy, K. R. Varshney, Optimized pre-processing for discrimination prevention, NIPS 30, 2017
edges.evidence: We chose five such algorithms (all from IBM AIF360) which we thought could be representative of the works done before. Table 4 shows the results

edges.target: Reweighing (Kamiran & Calders)
edges.ref: [32] F. Kamiran and T. Calders, Data preprocessing techniques for classification without discrimination, Knowledge and Information Systems 33(1), 2012
edges.evidence: Reweighing(Pre-processing)[32] ... In most of the cases, Fairway is performing better or the same with prior algorithms in case of reducing ethical bias (AOD,EOD)

edges.target: Adversarial Debiasing (Zhang, Lemoine, Mitchell)
edges.ref: [34] B. H. Zhang, B. Lemoine, and M. Mitchell, Mitigating unwanted biases with adversarial learning, 2018
edges.evidence: Adversial Debiasing[34] (In-processing) ... Like Fairway, previous algorithms also slightly damage the recall metric

edges.target: Reject Option Classification (Kamiran et al.)
edges.ref: [36] F. Kamiran, S. Mansha, A. Karim, and X. Zhang, Exploiting reject option in classification for social discrimination control, Inf. Sci., 2018
edges.evidence: Reject Option Classification[36] (Post-processing) ... In case of false alarm, Fairway has less number of black cells showing damage

edges.target: IBM AI Fairness 360 toolkit
edges.ref: [25] Ai fairness 360: An extensible toolkit for detecting, understanding, and mitigating unwanted algorithmic bias, 10 2018. https://github.com/IBM/AIF360
edges.evidence: We chose five such algorithms (all from IBM AIF360) which we thought could be representative of the works done before

edges.target: AIF360 result that prior methods damage performance
edges.ref: [25] Ai fairness 360: An extensible toolkit ..., 10 2018. https://github.com/IBM/AIF360
edges.evidence: IBM has created a GitHub repo to combine some promising prior works on fairness domain[25]. The results show that most of the prior methods damage the performance of the model

edges.target: EOD / AOD fairness metrics (Bellamy et al., AIF360)
edges.ref: [40] R. Bellamy et al., Ai fairness 360: An extensible toolkit for detecting, understanding, and mitigating unwanted algorithmic bias, 10 2018
edges.evidence: Equal Opportunity Difference(EOD): Difference of True Positive Rates(TPR) for unprivileged and privileged groups [40]. Average Odds Difference(AOD) ... [40]

edges.target: FLASH sequential model-based optimizer (Nair et al.)
edges.ref: [55] V. Nair, Z. Yu, T. Menzies, N. Siegmund, and S. Apel, Finding faster configurations using flash, TSE, 2018
edges.evidence: For our work, we modified FLASH and generated FAIR_FLASH that seeks best parameters for Logistic regression model with four goals

edges.target: FLASH faster than DE and NSGA-II (Nair et al.)
edges.ref: [55] V. Nair, Z. Yu, T. Menzies, N. Siegmund, and S. Apel, Finding faster configurations using flash, TSE, 2018
edges.evidence: FLASH was invented to solve software configuration problem and it performed faster than more traditional optimizers such as Differential Evolution[57] or NSGA-II[58]

edges.target: Bad learners rank configurations correctly (Nair et al.)
edges.ref: [56] V. Nair, T. Menzies, N. Siegmund, and S. Apel, Using bad learners to find good configurations, FSE 2017, pp. 257-267
edges.evidence: as shown by Nair et al., such guesses can rank guesses in (approximately) the same order as that generated by other, much slower, methods [56]

edges.target: Scikit-learn Logistic Regression
edges.ref: footnote 3: In Scikit-Learn, those details are C=1.0, penalty='l2', solver='liblinear', max_iter=100 (no reference entry)
edges.evidence: We trained a logistic regression model with default scikit-learn parameters and tested on the five datasets

edges.target: Situation testing (Zhang, Wu, Wu)
edges.ref: [31] L. Zhang, Y. Wu, and X. Wu, Situation testing-based discrimination discovery: A causal inference approach, IJCAI'16, pp. 2718-2724
edges.evidence: We used Situation testing [31] to verify whether after bias removal, the role of a protected attribute on the prediction changes or not

edges.target: UCI Adult Census Income dataset
edges.ref: [47] Uci:adult data set, 1994. http://mlr.cs.umass.edu/ml/datasets/Adult
edges.evidence: Adult Census Income - This dataset contains records of 48,842 people. The class label is yearly income [47]

edges.target: ProPublica COMPAS recidivism dataset
edges.ref: [48] propublica/compas-analysis, 2015. https://github.com/propublica/compas-analysis
edges.evidence: Compas - This is a dataset containing criminal history, demographics, jail and prison time, and COMPAS ... risk scores for defendants from Broward County [48]

edges.target: UCI German Credit dataset
edges.ref: [49] Uci:statlog (german credit data) data set, 2000. https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/Statlog+(German+Credit+Data)
edges.evidence: German Credit Data - This dataset contains records of 1,000 people and binary class labels (Good Credit or Bad Credit) [49]

edges.target: UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset
edges.ref: [50] Uci:default of credit card clients data set, 2016. https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/default+of+credit+card+clients
edges.evidence: Default Credit - There are 30,000 records of default payments of people from Taiwan [50]

edges.target: UCI Heart Disease dataset
edges.ref: [51] Uci:heart disease data set, 2001. https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/Heart+Disease
edges.evidence: Heart Health - The Heart Dataset from the UCI ML Repository contains fourteen features from 297 adults [51]

edges.target: Scott-Knott test and A12 effect size
edges.ref: (no reference entry given; named in text only)
edges.evidence: We have performed scott-knott significance test and A12 effect size test for comparison. For AOD, Fairway performs better in 2/5 cases

edges.target: 70/15/15 train-validation-test split
edges.ref: [54] Why split data in the ratio 70:30? 2012. http://informationgain.blogspot.com/
edges.evidence: we divided the dataset into three groups - Training (70%), Validation (15%) and Test (15%)[54]

edges.target: Definition of bias as systematic error (Martin)
edges.ref: [39] J. Martin, Bias or systematic error (validity), 2010. https://www.ctspedia.org/do/view/CTSpedia/BiasDefinition
edges.evidence: Martin argues (and we agree) that "bias is a systematic error" [39]

edges.target: Beutel et al. shortcomings of fairness metrics
edges.ref: [45] A. Beutel, J. Chen, T. Doshi, H. Qian, A. Woodruff, C. Luu, P. Kreitmann, J. Bischof, E. H. Chi, Putting fairness principles into practice, 2019
edges.evidence: Beutel et al. commented that all of these fairness metrics suffer from three shortcomings [45] ... In this work, several steps are taken to overcome those shortcomings

edges.target: Chen et al. - classifier bias comes from training data
edges.ref: [13] I. Chen, F. D. Johansson, and D. Sontag, Why is my classifier discriminatory? 2018
edges.evidence: Chen et al. mentioned that a model acquires bias from training data[13] ... Their work motivated us to find bias in the training data rather than model

edges.target: Berk et al. - fairness has a cost (accuracy-fairness trade-off)
edges.ref: [14] R. Berk, H. Heidari, S. Jabbari, M. Joseph, M. Kearns, J. Morgenstern, S. Neel, A. Roth, A convex framework for fair regression, 2017
edges.evidence: Berk et al. have stated that achieving fairness has a cost [14] ... following the idea of Berk et al, we apply multiobjective optimization approach

edges.target: Kamishima et al. Prejudice Remover / underestimation index
edges.ref: [35] T. Kamishima, S. Akaho, H. Asoh, J. Sakuma, Fairness-aware classifier with prejudice remover regularizer, ECML PKDD 2012, pp. 35-50
edges.evidence: They defined a new metric called the underestimation index (UEI) ... According to them, this occurs very rarely. So, we did not try to find UEI for our datasets
edges.section: 6.1 Why not Remove the Protected Attributes?

edges.target: Hardt et al. / prior fairness work used Logistic Regression
edges.ref: [38] M. Hardt, E. Price, and N. Srebro, Equality of opportunity in supervised learning, 2016
edges.evidence: Like most of the prior research[33, 35, 38], we used Logistic Regression model on these datasets

edges.target: Brun et al. - correlated attributes keep bias after removing protected attribute
edges.ref: [52] Fairware 2018: international workshop on software fairness. http://fairware.cs.umass.edu/
edges.evidence: Initially, we also thought maybe correlation is the reason for our datasets also. But when we checked for the correlation between attributes, we found that bias is not coming from the correlation
edges.section: 6.1 Why not Remove the Protected Attributes?

edges.target: THEMIS / Galhotra et al. (situation testing concept, dataset precedent)
edges.ref: [29] S. Galhotra, Y. Brun, and A. Meliou, Fairness testing: testing software for discrimination, ESEC/FSE 2017
edges.evidence: Instead of depending on only those two metrics, the concept of situation testing was used to find discrimination [29]

edges.target: Chakraborty et al. 2019 - SE for fairness with hyperparameter optimization
edges.ref: [46] J. Chakraborty, T. Xia, F. M. Fahid, and T. Menzies, Software engineering for fairness: A case study with hyperparameter optimization, 2019
edges.evidence: All the datasets are quite popular in fairness domain and used by previous SE researchers[29, 30, 46]

edges.target: Holstein et al. - practitioners struggle with ML fairness algorithms
edges.ref: [59] K. Holstein, J. Wortman Vaughan, H. Daume, M. Dudik, H. Wallach, Improving fairness in machine learning systems, CHI 2019
edges.evidence: Software practitioners having little ML knowledge may face difficulties to use these algorithms[59]. In case of Fairway, users can clearly see

not_reuse_examples: [30] Udeshi et al. AEQUITAS and [11] Aggarwal et al. black-box fairness testing: described in 2.3 but the paper explicitly says 'We did not use these methods'
[8] Brun & Meliou 'Software fairness' and [7] Angell et al.: background call-to-action that fairness is an SE problem; nothing executed or adopted
[15]-[21] news/anecdote citations (Google sentiment, YouTube captions, Amazon recruiting) and [22]-[24] IEEE/EU/Microsoft AI ethics principles: motivation only
[57] Storn & Price DE and [58] Deb et al. NSGA-II: named only as optimizers FLASH was previously compared against; not run here
notes: ESEC/FSE 2020 empirical method paper (Fairway = ambiguity removal + FAIR_FLASH tuning); self-reuses FLASH; text says 'five' AIF360 baselines but Table 4 lists four; Scott-Knott/A12 used without citation; several broken '[? ]' citations (figshare package, German et al.).
